analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop a disease-agnostic data model and pluggable module interface for spatio-temporal risk analytics, addressing the challenge of relying on isolated, disease-specific workflows for animal-health surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated an open-source Python reference implementation using raw anthrax and rabies registries with 4183 and 363 georeferenced records, respectively, to test the full registry-ingestion and modeling workflow.
analysis.methods: The system was tested with raw anthrax and rabies registries, and the PCA and Bayesian components used aggregates reconstructed from earlier publications to assess interface conformance and numerical reproduction.
analysis.main_results: The scan component reproduced the primary SaTScan clusters with Jaccard indices of 0.91 and 1.00, although it matched only 8 of 13 significant anthrax clusters. Spatial block cross-validation yielded AUC values of 0.74–0.77 for anthrax, compared with 0.67–0.70 for the elapid MaxEnt implementation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate the system's ability to run on a single workstation, highlighting its modular design and potential for integration into existing surveillance frameworks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the system can improve the efficiency and flexibility of spatio-temporal risk analytics for animal-health surveillance, supporting better disease monitoring and response strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not test database-backed deployment, operational scaling, or prospective forecasting, and the runtime gap applies only to specific implementations, feature sets, and datasets.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a disease-agnostic data model and pluggable module interface for spatio-temporal risk analytics, with an open-source Python reference implementation. The system was tested using raw anthrax and rabies registries, demonstrating its ability to reproduce SaTScan clusters and achieve moderate AUC values for risk prediction. The modular design allows for easy integration of new diseases, as evidenced by the minimal code changes required to add a fifth disease. However, the study did not evaluate operational scaling or prospective forecasting, limiting the generalizability of the findings. The results suggest that the system could enhance animal-health surveillance by enabling more flexible and efficient risk analysis workflows.

title: Microbiological safety assessment of canine adipose derived mesenchymal stem cell preparations reveal no detectable contamination
abstract: The experimental application of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (cAD-MSC) has demonstrated excellent therapeutic potential in the treatment of a number of previously untreatable or difficult-to-treat diseases. However, the production of cAD-MSC for clinical application necessitates in vitro isolation and cell expansion, introducing the risk of microbiological contamination. Studies indicate that stored MSCs may be contaminated with bacteria, fungi, or viruses, resulting in cell transformation, cell death, or persistent infection. This ultimately compromises therapeutic efficacy and potentially facilitates therapy-induced pathogen transmission. In accordance with the European Medicines Agency guidelines mandating sterility testing as an integral component of the manufacturing process, this study aimed to assess the sterility of the cAD-MSC bank at the Croatian Veterinary Institute. To test for the most clinically significant canine pathogens, nucleic acids were extracted from 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods. The pathogen screening panel included rabies virus (Lyssavirus), canine herpesvirus (Varicellovirus canidalpha1), parvovirus (Carnivore protoparvovirus 1), coronavirus (Alphacoronavirus 1), distemper virus (Morbillivirus canis), Rotavirus A, Leptospira spp, Brucella canis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Anaplasma spp, Ehrlichia spp, Mycoplasma spp (hemotropic), and Neospora caninum. No tested gene fragments of the aforementioned pathogens were detected, indicating that the cAD-MSC preparations were free from the presence of clinically significant pathogens. Rigorous implementation of sterility control during the cell isolation and expansion process is essential to ensure safe cell-based therapy in canine patients.

abstract_zh: 犬脂肪源性间充质干细胞/基质细胞(cAD-MSC)的实验应用已证明治疗对许多以前无法治疗或难以治疗的疾病具有优异的治疗潜力。然而,用于临床应用的cAD-MSC的生产需要体外分离和细胞扩增,从而引入微生物污染的风险。研究表明,储存的间充质干细胞可能被细菌、真菌或病毒污染,导致细胞转化、细胞死亡或持续感染。这最终会损害治疗效果并可能促进治疗诱导的病原体 传播。根据欧洲药品管理局指南,要求将无菌检测作为生产过程的一个组成部分,本研究旨在评估克罗地亚兽医研究所 cAD-MSC 库的无菌性。为了检测临床上最重要的犬病原体,从 32 个 cAD-MSC 制剂中提取核酸,并使用标准分子 PCR 方法进行分析。病原体筛查小组包括狂犬病病毒(狂犬病毒)、犬疱疹病毒(Varicellovirus canidalpha1)、细小病毒(Carnivore protoparvovirus 1)、冠状病毒(Alphacoronavirus 1)、犬瘟热病毒(Morbillivirus canis)、轮状病毒A、钩端螺旋体属、犬布鲁氏菌、伯氏疏螺旋体、无形体spp、埃利希体属、支原体属(嗜血性)和犬新孢子虫。没有检测到上述病原体的测试基因片段,表明cAD-MSC制剂不存在临床上显着的病原体。在细胞分离和扩增过程中严格实施无菌控制对于确保犬类患者的安全细胞治疗至关重要。

title: Chile eliminates dog-mediated rabies.

The validation recognises a programme that has maintained surveillance and response capacity despite the absence of human cases. Chile’s last reported case of human rabies transmitted by dogs was in 1972.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to eliminate dog-mediated rabies in Chile, addressing a long-standing public health issue. After over five decades without a human case transmitted by dogs, Chile has gained WHO validation for eliminating this disease.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved surveillance and response capacity maintenance in Chile, focusing on the absence of human cases of rabies transmitted by dogs since 1972.
elements_en.methods: Chile maintained surveillance and response capacity despite the absence of human cases of rabies transmitted by dogs, with the last reported case in 1972.
elements_en.main_results: Chile’s last reported case of human rabies transmitted by dogs was in 1972.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The validation recognises Chile’s programme for maintaining surveillance and response capacity, marking it as the first country in South America to eliminate dog-mediated rabies as a public health problem.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform future rabies control strategies, particularly in surveillance and response capacity maintenance, and highlight the importance of long-term commitment to public health measures.

title_zh: 智利消除了以狗为媒介的 狂犬病。
source_body_en: Chile is the first country in South America to gain WHO validation for eliminating dog-mediated rabies as a public health problem, after more than five decades without a human case transmitted by a dog. Chile’s last reported case of human rabies transmitted by dogs was in 1972.
